news_summary: Vistra reported mixed Q2 2026 results on Aug 7, 2026 (GAAP EPS missed consensus on a large unrealized hedge mark-to-market loss, but ongoing-operations adjusted EBITDA rose 31% year-over-year and full-year guidance was reaffirmed). The same week FERC approved Vistra's roughly $4 billion acquisition of Cogentrix's 5.5 GW gas fleet over market-monitor objections, and Vistra's Q2 release confirmed it is a founding, up-to-$1 billion power-partner investor in the newly launched KKR/NVIDIA-backed Helix Digital Infrastructure venture. Sell-side reaction to earnings was split, with some price targets raised and others cut.

catalysts.what: Vistra reported Q2 2026 results: GAAP net income $305M, EPS $0.76 (missed consensus, driven by a $472M/$488M unrealized mark-to-market loss on hedges), ongoing-operations adjusted EBITDA $1.767B (+31% YoY, vs $1.35B prior year). FY2026 guidance reaffirmed at $6.8B-$7.6B adjusted EBITDA and $3.925B-$4.725B adjusted free cash flow before growth.

FERC approved Vistra's roughly $4B acquisition of Cogentrix Energy's 5.5 GW gas-fired fleet (case EC26-63) despite objections from the ISO-NE and PJM (Monitoring Analytics) market monitors over horizontal market power. The deal still needs DOJ Hart-Scott-Rodino clearance and state approvals before closing, expected in H2 2026.

Vistra is a founding investor and preferred power provider in Helix Digital Infrastructure, a new AI-infrastructure venture launched with KKR, Kuwait Investment Authority and NVIDIA carrying $10B+ in long-duration committed capital; Vistra has committed up to $1.0 billion.

PJM's next Base Residual Auction (capacity auction), for the 2029/2030 Delivery Year, is scheduled for December 2026 as PJM works toward returning to its three-year-forward planning cycle; exact offer-window and results-posting dates have not yet been published. Vistra sells generation capacity into PJM's capacity market.

move_thesis: VST has been trading on the intersection of AI/data-center power demand and PJM capacity-market pricing. Bull-case drivers: adjusted EBITDA up 31% YoY, reaffirmed 2026 guidance, FERC clearance of the ~$4B Cogentrix acquisition (expanding PJM/ISO-NE/ERCOT gas capacity), and a new up-to-$1B commitment to the KKR/NVIDIA-backed Helix digital-infrastructure venture. Near-term overhangs: the quarter's GAAP EPS miss (largely a hedge mark-to-market accounting effect rather than an operating shortfall), a split round of post-earnings analyst price-target moves (Scotiabank raised, Wells Fargo and BofA cut), and press narratives questioning how durable data-center-driven power demand growth is. PJM's December 2026 Base Residual Auction (2029/2030 delivery year) is a structural forward catalyst for capacity revenue.
